public_health_question.v: What was the prevalence of SARS-CoV-2 infection among active duty soldiers deployed to care for COVID-19 patients at a NYC field hospital with a rigorous infection control plan?

ev.q: To assess the prevalence of SARS-CoV-2 infection among active duty soldiers deployed to JMS
SARS-CoV-2 Infection Risk Among Active Duty Military Members Deployed to a Field Hospital
A cross-sectional study of the prevalence of SARS-CoV-2 infection among 336 active duty soldiers enrolled in a prevalence study
All enrolled soldiers completed an anonymous study questionnaire that asked about demographic characteristics, duties at JMS
nasopharyngeal swabs were collected from all enrolled participants and were tested using the TaqPathTM COVID-19 Combo Kit
Deployed to a Field Hospital — New York City, April 2020

equity.level_reason: Only age and sex appear, as Table 1 characteristics and a median-age comparison of positive vs all soldiers, with no social-position framing. Professional role is an exposure route, not SES.

level_alternative.reason: The tested median-age contrast between infected and all soldiers could be read as an age-group-specific result, though age is not framed as social position.

notes: The prepass 'fisher' cue is Thermo Fisher Scientific, and 'sensitivity' refers to the assay, not to a diagnostic-accuracy study. PCR, ELISA and MMIA only define case status, so they are not procedures. The comparison with other health care personnel cohorts is cited from earlier studies.
view_issues: The Wilcoxon test compares the 6 positives with all 336 enrolled, which includes those 6, so the groups are not independent. Six of 336 is 1.8%, not the 1.7% reported. The text gives 99 medical support staff (27.9%), but Table 1 gives 94.
